correctness.rationale: For a conjugate-linear involution \(T\), expanding \(P_1=(T-\lambda_2I)/(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)\) while conjugating scalars shows \(P_1^2=P_1\); \(P_2=I-P_1\) is complementary and \(\lambda_1P_1+\lambda_2P_2=T\). For pointwise conjugation and phases \(1,i\), the projections reduce on \(u+iv\) to explicit real-linear lines, and the phase \(1,-1\) sends the constant \(i\) to \(2-i\), so it is not an isometry. The block calculation for Form IV gives \(T^2=I\) exactly when \(\phi^2=\mathrm{id}\) and \( eta(t)\overline{ eta(\phi(t))}=1\). These computations are direct and independently reconstruct the counterexample.
